The enhanced subscription service will add Smart Money analytics and Vega AI credits, giving active traders access to more market insights and tools within one platform

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Webull (NASDAQ: BULL), the online investment platform trusted by traders and investors worldwide, built on next-generation global infrastructure, today announced upcoming updates to Webull Premium. The subscription is designed to deliver greater value to active traders through a combination of advanced trading analytics, AI-powered research capabilities, and financial benefits.

Premium will introduce Smart Money tools and credits for select Vega AI features, expanding the resources available to subscribers for analyzing market activity, researching potential trading opportunities and evaluating market trends. The enhanced subscription also builds on existing financial benefits, including enhanced cash management rates, reduced margin rates, eligible index-options and futures fee discounts, and real-time market data.

The new Smart Money suite will provide subscribers with a collection of market-monitoring tools designed to deliver deeper insights into market activity, institutional positioning, and market trends. OrderFlow Lite analyzes large order buy and sell pressure to identify potential trends and reversals. Sage Tracker provides visibility into reported holdings and position changes across more than 9,000 institutions, including hedge funds. Signal Radar identifies stocks with notable price momentum and trading volume, while Net Premium Flow tracks options activity and order-flow patterns to help traders better understand market dynamics and sentiment.

"Active traders need access to timely market insights and analytical tools to evaluate investment opportunities and make informed decisions," said Anthony Denier, Group President and U.S. CEO of Webull. "With this update to Webull Premium, we're bringing together advanced trading tools, AI-powered research, and financial benefits in one subscription, making it easier for traders to access the resources they need through a single platform."

Premium will include AI credits that give subscribers access to select Vega AI features. These capabilities are designed to help traders streamline research, analyze market developments and gain additional insights as they evaluate potential opportunities.

The updated Premium will provide a more integrated alternative to purchasing individual research and analytics tools separately. OrderFlow Lite and Sage Tracker are included with Premium at no additional cost, while Signal Radar and Net Premium Flow are available through a seven-day free trial, extended to 45 days for annual subscribers, followed by a 50% discount for Premium members. The tools will also be available as standalone subscriptions.

Premium enhancements will be coming soon to eligible U.S. customers. Certain account types, including entity accounts, advisor accounts, and Managed IRAs, are not eligible.

The initiative launched with the first in a series of COSI HIVE events serving Central Ohio students.

COLUMBUS, Ohio, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Northwest Bank and the Center of Science and Industry (COSI) are helping Central Ohio students build practical financial skills and explore careers in banking through a new series of hands-on learning experiences.

The partnership officially launched at Ridgeview Middle School with a COSI HIVE (Human Innovation Experience) experience, a hands-on program that introduces students to real-world skills and careers through interactive activities. At the event, approximately 150 students went through five interactive stations led by COSI educators and Northwest Bank volunteers. At each station students explored financial concepts. They practiced budgeting while selecting materials to make slime and learned about risk management through a block-building exercise.

"Financial literacy is one of the most important life skills we can help foster in the communities we serve," said Devin Teles-Cygnar, chief marketing and communications officer and Northwest Bank Charitable Foundation president. "By teaming up with COSI, we have an opportunity to engage students in a meaningful way that helps build confidence, encourages curiosity and opens doors to future possibilities. Together, we're creating opportunities that help communities thrive."

Through a $125,000 contribution, Northwest will support additional HIVE events in four other Central Ohio communities served by the bank. 

"COSI believes learning is most powerful when it is relevant, engaging and connected to real-world opportunities and money is one of the first places young people engage in math in everyday life," said Dr. Frederic Bertley, president and CEO of COSI. "The HIVE-Fin-Lit edition was created on the premise that students deserve to see what is possible in the fields of mathematics, actuarial sciences and finance. Together with Northwest Bank, we can help students build financial confidence, explore future careers and develop the skills they need to succeed in our rapidly changing world. We are grateful to Northwest Bank for partnering with COSI to bring this important educational opportunity to students in the hometown we share."

Northwest will also support the development of a financial literacy learning kit created by COSI and the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland. The kit is designed to help families build practical skills in budgeting, saving, decision-making and financial planning.

This effort builds on Northwest's growing investment in Central Ohio. The bank recently opened its third Columbus financial center on Bethel Road, with new centers planned in Gahanna in December and Westerville in the first quarter of 2027 and a 75,000‑sq‑ft, purpose‑built corporate headquarters in Dublin, OH with relocation planned for 2029.

About Northwest Bank

Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, Northwest Bancshares, Inc. is the bank holding company of Northwest Bank. Founded in 1896, Northwest Bank is a full-service financial institution offering a complete line of business and personal banking products, as well as employee benefits and wealth management services. Currently, Northwest operates more than 150 full-service financial centers and 11 drive-up locations across Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, and Indiana and provides customers fee-free access to more than 55,000 ATMs. Additional information regarding Northwest Bancshares, Inc. and Northwest Bank can be accessed online at www.northwest.bank. 

About COSI

COSI, ranked "#1 Science Museum in the Country" six of the last seven years as voted by USA TODAY's 10Best, is an esteemed science center that has delighted Central Ohio with all things science for 60 years, inspiring interest in science, technology, engineering, arts, and math (STEAM) topics and delivering our experiential, "hands-on fun" brand of learning. COSI has been awarded 15 Emmy® Awards for its effective science communication television and video productions impacting science literacy for people of all ages. As a trusted educational resource for families, schools, and community partners, COSI is an essential element of our regional, national, and international communities, engaging millions of people annually through onsite, offsite, and online experiences. Learn more at www.cosi.org.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Better Home & Finance Holding Company (NASDAQ: BETR) today announced that two established mortgage advisors have joined NEO Home Loans, powered by Better. Brandon Goldberg leads Your Home Loan Surgeons in the greater San Diego market, and Ryan Davis is based in Lompoc, near Santa Barbara. Both advisors bring new purchase volume to Better and widen its reach in Southern California and on the Central Coast.

Your Home Loan Surgeons funded $30.1 million in loan volume during 2025, and 93% of that volume came from purchase loans. Goldberg has 17 years of mortgage experience in California and Texas and has built deep partnerships with realtors and the Building Industry Association in the greater San Diego market. His team focuses on helping builder and agent partners protect transactions and close with fewer surprises. He joins as a Mortgage Advisor alongside Production Partner Shauna Jensen.

Davis funded $20 million in loan volume over the past 12 months, and 56% of that volume came from purchase loans. He spent five years building his business in Lompoc, where he previously owned Oak and Vine Home Loans, and he joins as a Branch Leader and Mortgage Advisor. Both advisors’ referral relationships with local agents and builders complement Better’s direct-to-consumer business.

“Together, Brandon and Ryan funded $50 million in loan volume in 2025, and most of that was purchase business that came through agents and builders who trust them,” said Vishal Garg, Founder and Head of Platform, Product and Innovation at Better. “Brandon’s builder partners count on him to close on schedule. Ryan was doing his own post-closing paperwork. Our technology takes that operational work off their plates, so they can spend their time with borrowers and the partners who send them business.”

“I find it hard to trust people in this industry, and trust is the most important thing to me. Over a number of meetings, that trust developed with the team at NEO,” said Goldberg. “When I asked Ryan Grant why NEO joined Better, he said he saw what Better was doing and didn’t want to compete with all of its partnerships and technology. I feel the same way. The technology will add to the systems and processes I’ve built, and the model fits how I want to scale my team as I work with more builders.”

“As a business owner, I was managing every part of the process, and it took time away from the families I wanted to help,” said Davis. “NEO Home Loans powered by Better is investing in technology at a time when our industry is changing fast, and the culture of care, collaboration, accountability and doing the right thing made this the right place to build the next chapter of my business. I can focus on my clients and have a team and community behind me.”

“Growing NEO means investing in local professionals who understand their communities and have the relationships to make a real impact,” said Ryan Grant, President of NEO Home Loans, powered by Better. “By putting Better’s lead generation, technology and market share strategies behind Ryan, we’re giving him more ways to reach families, strengthen his partnerships with local agents and builders, and grow his business on the Central Coast.”

Built for scalability and operational efficiency, Benihana Express features a streamlined operating model designed for spaces of approximately 800 to 1,000 square feet. Its flexible format is suited for a wide range of traditional and nontraditional locations, including storefronts, airports, sports and entertainment venues, travel hubs and other high-traffic destinations. Record Volume and ADV Across North American Financial Power Options

NEW YORK & HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE), one of the world’s leading providers of financial market technology and data powering global capital markets, today announced that open interest (OI) across ICE’s North American financial power futures and options reached a record of over 1.7 billion megawatt hours, with options accounting for approximately one third at a record 573 million megawatt hours in November, up 13% year-over-year (y/y).

Traded volume across ICE’s North American financial power options hit a record 2 billion megawatt hours so far this year, already outpacing the total amount traded in 2025, while average daily volume (ADV) is at a record 9.1 million megawatt hours, with both volume and ADV up 25% y/y.

“Managing extreme weather, data center growth and tighter supply is now central to how participants approach North American power, and they are using ICE’s futures and options to price that risk,” said Brian Lewis, VP of North American Natural Gas and Power at ICE. “Options in particular have grown in importance as a flexible way to hedge exposure that is hard to size or time, which describes much of today’s power market. That is especially valuable as power demand grows in ways that are difficult to anticipate, and when heat waves, cold snaps and a thin supply cushion can stress the grid at short notice.”

Options growth has been driven by contracts covering the PJM Interconnection which operates the electric grid across 13 states and the District of Columbia, spanning the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, with ADV up 24% year-to-date (YTD). ICE’s ERCOT options, which allow market participants to manage electricity price risk in Texas, have also seen strong growth, with ADV up 82% YTD.

ICE offers the most comprehensive suite of power derivative products in the U.S., including over 400 financially settled futures and 60 options contracts, allowing market participants to hedge and manage risk at scale. As home to the largest and most liquid markets to trade energy derivatives, ICE’s markets cover global power, natural gas, freight and oil, alongside and environmental markets.

Mapped Macamic Fault Segments Total Approximately 30 km; Three High-Quality Exploration Blocks Across the Launay Property

 

TORONTO, ON – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 – Metalite Resources Inc. (CSE: METL) (OTC: JNCCF) (FSE: D680) ("Metalite" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the acquisition of additional mineral claims in Québec’s Launay district, expanding its northwestern exploration footprint along the Macamic Fault. The expansion encompasses 59 new claims and applications1 covering approximately 3,352 hectares and strengthens the Company’s position in the Macamic-Authier Block, one of three principal gold exploration areas being advanced at Launay.

The expansion follows Metalite’s fall 2026 exploration and ongoing historical-data compilation, which highlighted structural trends, geological contacts and preliminary responses warranting further investigation along the northwestern corridor.

"Our work this fall has given us a clearer basis for expanding Launay and deciding where to focus next," said Alex Storcheus, Executive Chairman of Metalite. "Macamic-Authier brings together an important stretch of the fault corridor, a historical silver-lead showing and a substantial body of exploration information that we can now examine as an integrated package. Together with the Chauvignet and Lyndhurst blocks, it gives us three distinct areas in which to test our geological ideas and build the next generation of exploration targets."

Three Blocks, a Shared Geological Framework

Metalite has organized its Launay exploration activities around three blocks. Their current mapped outlines cover approximately 14,000 hectares in total, with the following areas and principal features:  

  • Chauvignet Block (~5,015 ha). This central exploration block includes the flagship Trojan Zone, where 105 diamond drill holes have been reported, totalling approximately 21,826 metres.2 The extensive historical exploration provides a foundation for understanding the gold-exploration setting along the Macamic structural corridor and for evaluating sheared volcanic rocks, intrusive contacts and quartz-vein systems in the district.  

  • Macamic-Authier Block (~4,978 ha). The northwestern focus of the current expansion lies in the Macamic–Authier area, extending toward Taschereau. Its attraction combines the Macamic Fault corridor, the historical Chemin de Fer-Sud silver–lead showing, a substantial archive of geological and geophysical work, and practical road and nearby rail access. Parts of the mapped block remain subject to claim-application approval. 

  • Lyndhurst Block (~3,933 ha). The southeastern block includes the interpreted intersection area of the Lyndhurst and Macamic structural corridors, an important focus for examining how faults, volcanic contacts and alteration relate to one another. The predecessor’s 2021 airborne magnetic and VLF-EM survey covered the Lyndhurst grid, providing data for structural interpretation and follow-up.

Metalite’s GIS analysis of the regional SIGÉOM Macamic Fault trace identifies approximately 29.9 kilometres of mapped fault segments (shown in red on the accompanying map) within the three block outlines: ~7.9 km at Chauvignet; ~13.2 km at Macamic-Authier; and ~8.9 km at Lyndhurst. The Launay Property lies in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt, where volcanic rocks, intrusive contacts and major deformation zones provide the geological setting for the Company’s exploration strategy. Numerous historic gold showing have been identified in close proximity and adjacent to the faults and shears in the region, including the Macamic Fault. The Macamic structure is a regional northwest-trending sheared corridor. Historical work at Launay describes quartz–carbonate–tourmaline veining and sulphides in altered, sheared volcanic rocks associated with the fault system and its subsidiary structures. These relationships support investigating deformation, alteration and vein development together, rather than treating individual anomalies in isolation.  

As reported on October 28, 2026, Metalite’s integrated program combined satellite imagery, radar, terrain analysis, historical geological information and prospecting, supported by TerraEye’s specialist spectral work. The program identified multiple geological follow-up localities, including potential bedrock exposures, structural and contact relationships, and preliminary spectral responses requiring ground verification.  

This work, together with the continuing assessment of historical data, supported the decision to expand along the northwestern continuation of the Macamic structural corridor. The objective is to bring promising geological relationships into a coherent exploration program, with a view to evaluating the potential continuity of mineralization at a district scale.

   

Macamic-Authier Block: Bringing Historical Reports into a Modern Compilation

Metalite has identified, analysed and digitized 88 historical assessment reports whose mapped coverage overlaps the Macamic-Authier Block. The collection includes a significant body of geophysical information, together with geological mapping and drilling records. Bringing these sources into a common digital framework allows the Company to compare historical responses with mapped structures, mineral occurrences and the current claim configuration. Preliminary findings include:

  • Drilling. The compilation identifies 24 historical drill holes totalling approximately 3,606 metres directly within the Macamic-Authier Block3 

  • Chemin de Fer-Sud: A Historical Mineralized Showing. A 1962 report4 by Québec resident geologist Jean Dugas describes three principal quartz veins in chloritic schist, with pyrite and minor chalcopyrite and galena; tourmaline and carbonate were also observed in one vein. A historical sample from one of the veins was reported to return 0.17 g/t Au, 77 g/t Ag, 0.12% Cu and 1.15% Pb (these historic assay results have not been verified in the field by Metalite professionals). 

  • Road and Rail Access. The block benefits from road access in the Macamic-Authier-Taschereau area, with a railway within a few hundred metres of portions of the property.  

  • Public Land Tenure. Metalite estimates that approximately half of the outlined block overlies public land.

Historical logs and survey data are being digitized to identify what has been tested, where coverage is incomplete and which anomalies merit renewed examination. Metalite is also integrating historical geophysical and geochemical data to assess similarities and differences relative to the Trojan Zone and other areas of documented gold mineralization5.

Next Steps

Metalite continues to advance its comprehensive compilation and interpretation of historical geological, geophysical and drilling data across the Launay Property, integrating these datasets with the results of its 2026 exploration program to refine and prioritize prospective exploration targets. This ongoing work is being undertaken with a view to finalizing the Company's drill permit applications and advancing its most prospective areas toward drill testing. Metalite has been working closely with its geological and permitting consultants to complete the necessary technical documentation and regulatory submissions, with the objective of positioning the Company to undertake targeted drilling programs, subject to receipt of the required approvals and available funding.

The Company owns a 100% interest in the Arthurs Seat Silver-Antimony Project in New South Wales, Australia and a 100% interest in the Launay Gold Property, a district-scale gold project located in Québec's Abitibi Greenstone Belt. YARDLEY, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Savara Inc. (Nasdaq: SVRA), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has communicated that it will not meet the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of November 22, 2026 for the Company’s molgramostim inhalation solution (molgramostim) Biologics License Application (BLA) for the treatment of autoimmune PAP. The review of the BLA is ongoing and no revised action date has been provided by the agency.

“We appreciate the FDA’s continued efforts on our application and look forward to working closely with the agency to complete its review,” said Matt Pauls, J.D., M.B.A., Chair and Chief Executive Officer, Savara.

About Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (Autoimmune PAP)

Autoimmune PAP is a rare lung disease characterized by the abnormal build-up of surfactant in the alveoli. Surfactant consists of proteins and lipids and is an important physiological substance that lines the alveoli to prevent them from collapsing. In a healthy lung, excess surfactant is cleared and digested by immune cells called alveolar macrophages. Alveolar macrophages need to be stimulated by granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) to function properly in clearing surfactant, but in autoimmune PAP, GM-CSF is neutralized by autoantibodies against GM-CSF, rendering macrophages unable to adequately clear surfactant. As a result, an excess of surfactant accumulates in the alveoli, causing impaired gas transfer, resulting in clinical symptoms of shortness of breath, often with cough and frequent fatigue. Patients may also experience episodes of fever, chest pain, or coughing up blood, especially if secondary lung infection develops. In the long term, the disease can lead to serious complications, including lung fibrosis and the need for a lung transplant.

About Molgramostim

Molgramostim inhalation solution (molgramostim) is an investigational recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in development for the treatment of autoimmune PAP. Molgramostim is delivered via an investigational eFlow® Nebulizer System (PARI Pharma GmbH), specifically developed for inhalation of molgramostim. The safety and efficacy of molgramostim have not been established, and it is not approved by the FDA or any other regulatory authority.

About Savara

Savara is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases. Our lead program, molgramostim (molgramostim inhalation solution), is a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in development for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (aPAP). Molgramostim is delivered via a proprietary investigational eFlow® Nebulizer System (PARI Pharma GmbH) specifically developed for inhalation of molgramostim. IRVINE, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / enVVeno Medical Corporation (Nasdaq:NVNO) ("enVVeno Medical" or the "Company"), a company setting new standards of care for the treatment of deep venous disease, will present three-year data from SAVVE, the U.S. pivotal study of the VenoValve® today at the 53rd Annual Vascular and Endovascular Issues, Techniques and Horizons (VEITH) Symposium in New York City. The data, which will be presented by Dr. David Dexter of Sentara Vascular Specialists, shows sustained, statistically significant improvements in the revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), leg pain and quality-of-life measures in patients with severe chronic venous insufficiency (CVI). The presentation will also highlight enVVe®, the Company's next-generation, non-surgical transcatheter replacement venous valve.

Among the data being presented at VEITH are:

  • 5.8-point average improvement in disease severity, as measured by rVCSS, from baseline to 36 months.
  • 18-point and 19-point average improvements in venous disease-specific quality of life (VEINES-QOL) and symptoms (VEINES-Sym), respectively.

The rVCSS is a clinically validated scoring system used to track the progression or regression of venous diseases, and a 5.8-point improvement represents a real difference in the daily lives of these patients. Improvement was observed as early as three months following implantation and was sustained through 36 months.

"Patients improved significantly after receiving the VenoValve, and this three-year data shows that those benefits have been sustained," said Robert Berman, Chief Executive Officer of enVVeno Medical. "Demonstrating the long-term viability of our replacement venous valve technology is critically important as we advance enVVe."

enVVe, the Company's next-generation, non-surgical replacement venous valve, builds on the clinical experience gained with VenoValve. Unlike VenoValve, which requires an open surgical procedure and an overnight hospital stay, enVVe is designed to be implanted in a less invasive procedure performed under light sedation, with patients expected to go home the same day.

enVVe will be evaluated in TAVVE (TrAnscatheter Venous Valve Endoprosthesis), a prospective, multicenter pivotal study that received FDA Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) authorization in April 2026. Part 1 of the TAVVE pivotal study will consist of up to 10 patients who will initially be monitored for safety. Following FDA review, the Company plans to proceed to Part 2 of the TAVVE pivotal study, which will evaluate regurgitant flow volume and rVCSS, along with other secondary endpoints. The Company remains on track to enroll the first patient in TAVVE by year-end 2026.

About the enVVe System

The investigational enVVe System is a transcatheter-delivered replacement venous valve designed to restore one-way blood flow in the deep veins of patients with chronic venous insufficiency. An estimated 3 million people in the U.S. suffer from severe deep venous insufficiency, and it remains one of the largest unmet needs in vascular medicine. As venous valves fail, patients often experience chronic pain, swelling, skin changes, recurrent venous leg ulcers and declining quality of life.

Despite the significant burden of deep venous insufficiency, treatment options remain limited and are primarily focused on managing symptoms through compression therapy and wound care rather than addressing the underlying cause: dysfunctional venous valves. The enVVe System is being developed to address this critical treatment gap by helping restore proper directional blood flow to the deep venous system.

About the SAVVE Study

The SAVVE (Surgical Anti-reflux Venous Valve Endoprosthesis) study is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter U.S. pivotal clinical study evaluating VenoValve in 75 patients with severe chronic venous insufficiency due to deep venous reflux across 21 U.S. clinical centers. The study includes patients with CEAP clinical classifications C4b through C6 and evaluates changes in disease severity, pain, quality of life, symptoms, venous ulcer area and device patency, with follow-up extending to five years.

About enVVeno Medical Corporation

enVVeno Medical (NASDAQ:NVNO) is an Irvine, California-based, late clinical-stage medical device company focused on the advancement of innovative bioprosthetic (tissue-based) solutions to improve the standard of care for the treatment of deep venous disease.

BERLIN, MD / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Calvin B. Taylor Bankshares, Inc. (OTCQX:TYCB), parent company of Calvin B. Taylor Bank (the "Bank"), announced a $125,000 commitment to Diakonia's Supportive Living Campus Capital Campaign.

The $15.25 million project will expand Diakonia's ability to serve Maryland's Lower Eastern Shore by bringing key programs and services together on one campus. The facility will include an expanded Food Pantry, Veteran Support and Outreach Center, Thrift Store, administrative offices, and, in a future phase, 42 units of supportive housing. Diakonia's Emergency Shelter will continue operating from its current location in West Ocean City.

"Taylor Bank has always believed in investing in the communities we serve, and Diakonia's Supportive Living Campus represents an opportunity to make a lasting difference right here at home," said M. Dean Lewis, Chief Executive Officer and President of Taylor Bank. "We've been proud to stand alongside Diakonia throughout this journey, and we're excited to see this vision becoming a reality for the individuals and families who need it most."

"Dean Lewis and the entire Taylor Bank team have been beside us since the beginning, and their leadership has been a crucial part of this project's success," said Ken Argot, Executive Director of Diakonia. "Their $125,000 investment is a tremendous show of confidence in our mission and the future of the Supportive Living Campus. We're incredibly grateful for their continued partnership and commitment to our community."

Taylor Bank is proud to invest in a project that will expand resources, housing opportunities, and support services across the Lower Eastern Shore. To learn more about Diakonia's Supportive Living Campus, visit www.diakoniaoc.org.

About Calvin B. Taylor Bank
Calvin B. Taylor Bank, the banking subsidiary of Calvin B. Taylor Bankshares, Inc. (OTCQX: TYCB), has been a trusted financial partner on the Delmarva Peninsula since its founding in 1890. Headquartered in Berlin, Maryland, the Bank provides a full suite of commercial and consumer banking services, including loans, deposit products, and modern payment solutions tailored to meet the evolving needs of its customers.

With 12 full-service branches across Maryland, Delaware, and Virginia, and Loan Production Offices in Salisbury, Maryland, and Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, Taylor Bank offers responsive service built on personal relationships, with experienced local bankers who make decisions right here in the community. Revenue up 11.5%, gross margin 83.3% and income from operations up 23.7%. 

REDWOOD CITY, CA , Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Biotricity Inc. (OTCQB: BTCY) ("Biotricity" or the "Company"), a medical technology company providing remote cardiac monitoring solutions, announced its financial results for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended September 30, 2026.

Dr. Waqaas Al-Siddiq, Biotricity Founder and CEO, said, "Our second quarter delivered year-over-year growth in technology fee revenue, a higher gross margin and operating leverage. Revenue grew 11.5%, gross margin expanded to 83.3% and income from operations rose 23.7%, as gross profit growth outpaced higher operating expenses, including the timing of research and development activities."

Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Highlights (compared to the second quarter of fiscal 2026)

  • Revenue increased 11.5% to $4.33 million. Technology fee revenue, the majority of which is recurring, increased 13.3% to $3.98 million, or 91.8% of total revenue (prior-year quarter: 90.4%).
  • Gross margin improved to 83.3% from 81.9%, driven by technology fee gross margin of 85.5% (prior-year quarter: 82.3%). Gross profit increased 13.4% to $3.61 million.
  • Operating expenses increased 12.5% to $3.27 million, primarily due to a 46.7% increase in research and development expenses to $0.88 million; selling, general and administrative expenses increased 3.5% from increased sales. Income from operations increased 23.7% to $339 thousand, an operating margin of 7.8% (prior-year quarter: 7.0%).
  • Net loss before dividends was $0.81 million (prior-year quarter: $0.69 million), including a $151 thousand non-cash loss on the change in fair value of derivative liabilities. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $0.95 million, or $(0.046) per share, compared to $0.77 million, or $(0.029) per share, on fewer weighted average shares.

Six-Month Highlights (compared to the prior-year period)

  • Revenue increased 11.0% to $8.61 million, driven by an 18.3% increase in technology fee revenue. Gross margin improved to 82.9% from 81.2%.
  • Net loss before dividends was $1.77 million (prior-year period: $1.36 million). Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $2.02 million, or $(0.092) per share, compared to $1.53 million, or $(0.057) per share.
  • Net cash provided by operating activities was $511 thousand (prior-year period: $42 thousand), primarily reflecting higher accounts payable, accrued liabilities and collections of accounts receivable.

Corporate Developments

  • The Company signed a national distribution agreement, subject to a successful pilot program, where the partner will fund commercial expansion in exchange for a 30% distribution margin. The 18-month pilot was officially kicked off in October and is restricted to 6 states. Upon a successful pilot, the program will be expanded.
  • In October 2026, the Company was selected to provide cardiac screenings to patients in low-income communities and developing countries under a charitably funded program. The Company will be paid in advance at its standard commercial rates and currently expects the program to involve the deployment of at least 1,000 devices; there can be no assurance as to the timing or extent of deployment or the revenue ultimately recognized.
  • Successfully established a long-term inventory financing program to fund production.

Full results are included in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed on November 16, 2026 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and available at www.sec.gov.

About Biotricity Inc.

Biotricity is reforming the healthcare market by bridging the gap in remote monitoring and chronic cardiac care. Doctors and patients trust Biotricity's unparalleled standard for preventive & personal care, including diagnostic and post-diagnostic solutions for cardiac conditions. The Company develops comprehensive remote health monitoring solutions for the medical and consumer markets. To learn more, visit www.biotricity.com.

Third-quarter SaaS revenue increases 25% with approximately 82% gross margin; resale revenue grows 19%

September restructuring expected to generate approximately $793,000 in annualized cost savings

Company continues evaluating potential defense technology acquisitions as part of its strategic diversification initiative

AIRPORT CITY, Israel, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MySize, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYSZ) ("MySize" or the "Company"), a technology-driven company operating across fashion e-commerce, AI-powered sizing solutions, resale and brand distribution, today announced its financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

For the first nine months of 2026, MySize generated revenue of $7.32 million, representing an increase of approximately 21% compared with $6.06 million in the corresponding period of 2025. Growth was primarily attributable to increased resale platform revenue and the inclusion of additional business activities in the Company's consolidated results.

Third-quarter revenue totaled $1.86 million, compared with $2.57 million in the prior-year period, a decrease of approximately 28%, reflecting lower Amazon sales due primarily to reduced inventory availability. Despite this decline, the Company's SaaS and resale segments continued to deliver year-over-year revenue growth.

During the quarter, MySize also advanced operational restructuring initiatives aimed at reducing its cost base, improving resource allocation and preserving liquidity, while continuing to evaluate opportunities to diversify its business through potential acquisitions in the defense technology sector.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

  • SaaS growth: SaaS Solutions revenue increased 25% year over year to $240,000, with gross margin of approximately 82%.
  • Resale momentum: Resale platform revenue increased approximately 19% to $413,000, compared with $347,000 in the prior-year quarter.
  • Operational restructuring: In September, MySize reduced the workforce at its Naiz Fit subsidiary by approximately 50%, which the Company estimates will result in annualized gross cost savings of approximately $793,000.
  • Capital raising: The Company completed a private placement in September 2026, generating approximately $2.5 million in gross proceeds and $2.12 million in net proceeds.
  • Strategic diversification: MySize continued evaluating potential acquisition opportunities in defense technology, consistent with the strategic initiative announced in September 2026.

Management Commentary

"2026 has been a period of important operational and strategic decisions for MySize," said Ronen Luzon, Chief Executive Officer of MySize.

"While our third-quarter results reflected inventory-related challenges in our Amazon business, we continued to see encouraging growth in our SaaS and resale operations. These results reinforce the importance of focusing our resources on businesses with differentiated capabilities and improving their operating economics.

"We have taken meaningful steps to streamline our organization, including a restructuring of Naiz Fit that we estimate will reduce annualized gross operating costs by approximately $793,000. Our immediate priorities remain disciplined cost management, liquidity preservation and more efficient capital allocation.

"At the same time, we are evaluating opportunities to expand beyond our traditional fashion technology and commerce activities. In particular, we see potential strategic opportunities in the defense technology sector, where we are assessing businesses with differentiated technologies and opportunities for long-term growth.

"Our objective is to build a more focused and financially sustainable organization while maintaining the flexibility to pursue transactions that we believe could create long-term shareholder value. We recognize the challenges reflected in our current financial performance and remain focused on execution, financial discipline and identifying the right strategic opportunities."

Strategic Diversification and Defense Technology Initiative

As previously announced in September 2026, MySize is evaluating potential acquisitions in the defense technology sector as part of a broader initiative to diversify its business portfolio and explore additional sources of long-term value creation.

The Company intends to evaluate potential opportunities based on factors including technological differentiation, commercial prospects, strategic fit, capital requirements and potential benefits to shareholders.

Any potential transaction would remain subject to satisfactory due diligence, financing availability, negotiation of definitive agreements, applicable regulatory and corporate approvals, Nasdaq requirements, and other customary conditions.

There can be no assurance that the Company's evaluation of potential opportunities will result in any completed acquisition. The Company does not undertake to disclose further developments unless and until a definitive agreement is executed or disclosure is otherwise required.

Operational Efficiency and Cost Optimization

During September 2026, MySize implemented a workforce reduction at Naiz Fit as part of its efforts to align operating expenses with current business conditions.

The restructuring is expected to generate approximately $793,000 in annualized cost savings, although the timing and amount of realized savings may differ from current estimates.

The Company continues to review its operating structure and resource allocation across its existing businesses, with an emphasis on managing inventory, controlling expenses and preserving cash.

Management expects these initiatives to support a more efficient operating structure, although the Company continues to face significant operating and liquidity challenges.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $1.86 million, compared with $2.57 million for the corresponding period in 2025, a decrease of approximately 28%. The decline was primarily attributable to lower Amazon sales resulting from reduced inventory levels.

Gross profit was $591,000, compared with $1.01 million in the prior-year period. Gross margin was approximately 31.8%, compared with 39.2%.

Research and development expenses increased to $238,000 from $131,000, primarily reflecting higher subcontractor expenses and investments in AI tools.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased to $706,000 from $1.23 million, primarily due to lower Amazon fees associated with reduced sales activity.

General and administrative expenses increased to $1.32 million from $1.00 million, primarily reflecting the inclusion of TenPeaks' expenses in the consolidated results.

Total operating expenses were approximately $2.27 million, compared with $2.37 million in the prior-year quarter.

Operating loss was $1.68 million, compared with $1.36 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Net loss was $1.80 million, compared with $1.34 million in the prior-year quarter.

Nine-Month 2026 Financial Results

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased approximately 21% to $7.32 million, compared with $6.06 million for the corresponding period of 2025.

Gross profit was $2.50 million, compared with $2.55 million in the prior-year period, and gross margin declined to approximately 34.2% from approximately 42.1%.

Operating loss was $4.80 million, compared with $3.00 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Net loss was $5.03 million, compared with $2.85 million for the first nine months of 2025.

Balance Sheet and Liquidity

As of September 30, 2026, MySize held approximately $2.28 million in cash and cash equivalents and $130,000 in restricted cash, representing combined cash balances of approximately $2.41 million, compared with $2.56 million as of December 31, 2025.

Net cash used in operating activities for the first nine months of 2026 was approximately $3.04 million, compared with $2.81 million in the prior-year period.

In September 2026, the Company completed a private placement with gross proceeds of approximately $2.50 million and net proceeds of approximately $2.12 million.

The Company expects continued operating losses and negative operating cash flows for the foreseeable future. Based on projected cash flows and cash balances as of September 30, 2026, management believes existing cash will be sufficient to fund operations for less than 12 months. Accordingly, substantial doubt exists regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern.

MySize will require additional capital in the near term to support its operations and potential strategic initiatives. There can be no assurance that additional financing will be available on acceptable terms or at all.

Outlook

Looking ahead, MySize's priorities include improving operational efficiency, managing inventory more effectively, reducing expenses and preserving liquidity across its existing businesses.

The Company also intends to continue evaluating strategic opportunities that may support its longer-term diversification objectives, including potential acquisitions in defense technology.

Management remains focused on balancing immediate financial and operational requirements with the evaluation of opportunities that could strengthen the Company's business portfolio over time.

About MySize, Inc.

MySize, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYSZ) operates businesses across fashion e-commerce, AI-powered sizing technology, resale and brand distribution. Its portfolio includes Orgad, Naiz Fit, Percentil and TenPeaks.

The Company is also evaluating strategic opportunities to diversify its business activities, including potential acquisitions in the defense technology sector.

For more information, visit www.mysizeid.com.

Words such as "expect," "anticipate," "intend," "plan," "believe," "estimate," "evaluate," "seek," "may," "will," "could," "potential" and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements.

These statements include, among other matters, expectations regarding operational restructuring, anticipated cost savings, future operating performance, liquidity, financing needs, strategic diversification, potential acquisitions in the defense technology sector and opportunities for long-term shareholder value creation.

Forward-looking statements are based on current expectations, estimates and assumptions and are subject to significant risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied.

Such risks include, among others, the Company's ability to obtain additional financing and the dilution that may result; its history of operating losses and negative cash flows; its ability to continue as a going concern; its ability to maintain compliance with Nasdaq continued listing requirements; its dependence on Amazon and changes in inventory availability, supply and customer demand; the execution and effects of restructuring initiatives and the realization of anticipated cost savings; the integration and performance of acquired businesses, including TenPeaks; the availability and suitability of acquisition targets; the ability to complete due diligence and negotiate definitive agreements; risks associated with entering the defense technology sector, in which the Company has no operating experience, including export control, government contracting, security clearance and foreign investment regulatory requirements; regulatory, corporate and stockholder approval requirements; political, economic and military conditions in Israel and the region; and currency exchange rate fluctuations.

WEST PALM BEACH, FL AND MIAMI, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ:ONDS) ("Ondas" or the "Company"), a leading provider of advanced autonomous systems and next-generation defense and security technologies, today shared highlights from the Ondas Defense Technology Summit, a small, invitation-only executive session held November 18 in Las Vegas co-hosted by Ondas, Palantir Technologies Inc. (Nasdaq:PLTR) and Regna AI. Executives and leaders from technology and defense companies, including Ondas, Palantir, Regna AI and Aston Martin Performance Technologies, along with other defense technology and AI innovators and industry experts, spent the day tackling the hardest question in defense today: how to turn AI, autonomy and advanced manufacturing at scale into capability the warfighter can count on.

The focused, executive-level format allowed for candid conversations about AI across defense missions, including sovereign AI. The summit reflects Ondas' strategy of bringing together the software, autonomous platforms and production capability that modern warfare requires.

The day opened with remarks from Ryan Hartman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Ondas Sentinel and Interim Chief Executive Officer of Regna AI. Palantir followed with a demonstration and presentation on sovereign AI for mission-critical operations. Four panels covered autonomy in the air and at sea and where unmanned systems go next, investing in defense tech, how industry and the Department of Defense partner to deliver, and defense tech capital markets and mergers and acquisitions. The day closed with Q&A and closing remarks from Hartman.

The summit coincided with Ondas' announcement of its "Speed to Decision" Global Partner relationship with Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team. Formula One is one of the most technology-driven sports in the world, and the engineering, data and rapid manufacturing developed for the track are increasingly being applied in other industries. Building on that experience, Bob Bell, Business Development Consultant at Aston Martin Performance Technologies, led the session on Manufacturing and Supply Chains for Defense, sharing lessons from the Formula One paddock on scaling production that can translate to the defense industrial base.

"Defense technology is attracting growing demand and investment, and capital is following the companies that can pair AI and autonomy with the ability to manufacture at scale," said Eric Brock, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Ondas Inc. "Convening leaders from technology, defense and capital markets with Palantir and Regna AI reflects how Ondas is positioning itself at the center of that shift, turning innovation into fielded capability and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

"Together, we're helping our defense partners deploy sovereign AI on their own terms, with control over their data and operations," said Elias Davis, Office of the CEO at Palantir Technologies. "Co-hosting the Summit with Ondas and Regna AI reflects our deep and expanding partnership."

"Bringing these leaders into one room let us focus on how AI is changing the mission and what it will take to get capability into the field sooner," said Ryan Hartman. "Across the demo and the panels, the message was consistent: AI and autonomy only matter if operators can trust them, control them and rely on them. That is where industry and government have to keep working side by side."

About Ondas Inc.

Ondas Inc. (Nasdaq:ONDS) is a leading provider of autonomous systems, robotics, and mission-critical technologies for defense, homeland security, public safety, critical infrastructure, and industrial markets. Board of Directors Cite Progress on and Acceleration of 2.0 Strategy

Phunware 2.0 Supported by Strong Leadership Team,
Balance Sheet and Liquidity

Company Urges Stockholders to Vote “FOR” Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE Proxy Card

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phunware, Inc. (“Phunware” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PHUN), a mobile-first AI-enabled guest intelligence platform company focusing on hotels, resorts, health systems and other large complex properties, has filed its definitive proxy statement and today issued a letter from its Board of Directors (the “Board”) to stockholders ahead of the Company’s 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders (the “Annual Meeting”), which will be held virtually on December 17, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time.

The letter outlines the recommendation of the Board’s Special Committee on Election Matters for stockholders to re-elect Board Chairperson Elliot Han for another term as a Class II director, the Company's progress and prospects under its 2.0 Strategy, and its responses to the proxy materials filed by Goldenwise Capital Group Limited (“Goldenwise”). Shareholders of record as of October 19, 2026, are entitled to vote at the Annual Meeting.

What You Need to Know Before You Vote.

At the December 17, 2026 Annual Meeting, stockholders will vote on a nominee to fill one Board seat. The Special Committee urges you to vote “FOR” Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card.

  • Mr. Han has played a key role in strengthening Phunware’s finances and leadership. He championed the approximately $104 million capital raise in 2024 that resolved liquidity challenges. As of September 30, 2026, Phunware held approximately $86.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, with no debt. Further, as Chairperson, led the appointment of Dmitry Kroshka as permanent CEO, ending a period of interim leadership.
  • Goldenwise has not made a convincing case. It has not made any proposals establishing how replacing Mr. Han would improve Phunware’s new strategy, customer acquisition, product commercialization, recurring revenue growth or other critical performance metrics. Stockholders deserve a clear explanation of how Goldenwise’s nominee would improve the Company and its prospects.
  • Mr. Ding’s disclosure record raises serious questions. He answered “No” when asked whether he had been involved in any prior proceedings involving allegations of a breach of fiduciary duty or similar conduct, despite being named in a 2020 lawsuit alleging professional negligence and breach of fiduciary duty involving approximately $1.3 million in alleged investment losses. Separately, Goldenwise only provided more fullsome public disclosure of its short call and short put options after Phunware questioned the accuracy and completeness of these disclosures. Shareholders deserve complete and accurate information from Goldenwise as they are being asked to vote in favor of its nominee for the Board.
  • Ms. Zhang’s commercial ties and track record warrant scrutiny. Her firm, Trunity Partners, had a business relationship with Goldenwise in 2025, and she served alongside Mr. Ding on Moberg Pharma’s board for just under eight months, where she was not re-elected in May 2026. Her independence from Goldenwise and what relevant experience she would bring to Phunware’s Board deserve scrutiny.
  • An independent review concluded Mr. Han is the stronger choice. A Special Committee of independent directors, with Mr. Han recused, evaluated both candidates. He brings a wealth of relevant public-market leadership experience, capital-markets and finance expertise, legal training, governance experience as Audit Committee chair and audit committee financial expert, and a hands-on role shaping and implementing the Phunware 2.0 Strategy. Ms. Zhang’s background is not additive to the Board’s aggregate skillset. Mr. Han’s extensive knowledge of Phunware 2.0 supports continuity as the Company works to convert its investments into signed customer agreements and recurring revenues.

How to Vote

Vote FOR Elliot Han only, on the WHITE proxy card, by Internet, telephone or mail, by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 16, 2026. Discard any GOLD card: a later-dated GOLD card cancels your WHITE vote. Questions? Call Alliance Advisors toll-free at 1-888-244-0487.

Letter to Stockholders

Dear Stockholders:

We believe Phunware is at a critical point in its evolution and transition. The Phunware Board and management team have been strengthened, a new vision and strategy referred to as “Phunware 2.0” is now being implemented, and the related hospitality and healthcare intelligence platforms, modules and products are in development. We are very focused on finalizing and adopting our 2027 operating plan and budget for Phunware 2.0 and completing and converting our 2.0 Strategy into revenues and enterprise value for our stockholders. We believe that continuity and uninterrupted execution at the top are very important to completing the 2.0 Strategy and ensuring those investments turn into growth for stockholders.

At Phunware’s 2026 Annual Meeting on December 17, 2026, stockholders will elect one Class II director to a three-year term. The Board’s nominee is Chairperson Elliot Han. Goldenwise Capital Group Limited, a Hong Kong-based investment manager led by its founder Mr. Huakun Richard Ding, has put forward Ms. Xuan Zhang in opposition to Mr. Han.

Stockholders should carefully examine the record, relationships, and objectives of anyone seeking Board influence. Mr. Ding began engaging with Phunware only this year. Against that limited history (and as discussed in more detail below), the discrepancy in his signed director questionnaire, Ms. Zhang’s commercial ties to Goldenwise and Mr. Ding, and the absence of a specific operating plan or alternative strategy presented by Mr. Ding warrant heightened scrutiny before stockholders entrust his nominee with a seat on the Board. In our view, Goldenwise has been far more specific about the Board influence it wants than the value its nominee would create for Phunware and its stockholders.

The question is not whether Ms. Zhang has useful qualifications: the question is whether replacing Mr. Han would make the Board stronger and improve Phunware and its prospects. The Board’s Special Committee on Election Matters concluded it would not, by concluding, among other items, that:

Mr. Han has delivered. He championed a capital raising strategy that resolved near-term liquidity challenges in 2024; he led the Board’s appointment of a permanent CEO, ending a period of interim leadership, paired with the installment of fuller executive bench; and he strongly supported and provided oversight and guidance on a near daily basis for implementation of our new Phunware 2.0 Strategy. Mr. Han went above and beyond to use his first term to lay a strong foundation for future growth, and his renomination ensures the Board can build on it without disruption.

Goldenwise has offered no plan. Despite repeated Board invitations to do so, Goldenwise failed to present any other specific operating plan or alternative strategy for Phunware. Goldenwise now appears to support the 2.0 Strategy, and require an operating plan and budget, with spending requirements and dated milestones - all of which the Board intends to do for 2027.

The Special Committee recommends that you vote FOR Chairperson Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card.

Why the Special Committee Recommends Elliot Han

Mr. Han has served on the Board as an independent director since January 2024 and as Chairperson since October 2025. He also chairs the Audit Committee and is designated an audit committee financial expert. His experience includes senior roles at Cantor Fitzgerald, the New York Stock Exchange, and Goldman Sachs, in addition to practicing corporate law at Freshfields. He is currently the Chief Investment Officer of C1 Fund Inc., a publicly traded closed-end investment fund, and a Partner at PGP Capital Advisors.

For stockholders, we believe the most important qualifications for a director at Phunware are:

  • Direct knowledge of Phunware’s business, technology, and 2.0 Strategy to challenge and support management and evaluate execution.
  • Financial and transactional expertise to oversee funding decisions, capital allocation, and inorganic growth.
  • Governance and leadership experience to support effective oversight and transparency as the Company moves forward.

As a Board member, Mr. Han advocated for and facilitated Phunware’s completion and utilization of its 2024 at-the-market equity financing program, through which the Company raised approximately $104 million. This capital addressed significant near-term liquidity needs and materially strengthened Phunware’s balance sheet and reduced debt, providing Phunware with the financial flexibility to pursue a strategic reset, adapt to macro headwinds, invest in strategy and product development, and evaluate inorganic growth opportunities. Since the commencement of his Board chairmanship in October 2025, Mr. Han helped develop and advance the Company's strategic pivot to Phunware 2.0, pushing Phunware from a legacy wayfinding and enterprise mobile development company to the AI-powered Guest Intelligence Platform phase and enabling execution of the strategy by helping appoint Dmitry Kroshka as permanent CEO and assembling an experienced product, marketing, sales, and finance team of employees and senior advisors to implement Phunware 2.0. He sharpened the Company’s focus and promoted operating discipline around defined platforms and related modules, products and customer propositions.

Importantly, Mr. Han’s contributions to the Board and the Company extend beyond financing and strategy. He has chaired the Compensation Committee, during which time he helped oversee CEO succession and disciplined executive and employee incentives, including conserving capital and aligning leadership incentives with the Company’s turnaround and performance. He has chaired the Audit Committee, during which he oversaw financial reporting, external audits, compliance, and risk controls. He has also led the Strategic Transactions Committee’s oversight of potential acquisitions and capital deployment. Mr. Han demonstrated leadership during a transformational turnaround period, navigating the Company through organizational changes and overseeing the Company’s responses to litigation matters while limiting management distraction. His level of commitment has been demonstrated through his attendance at all Board and committee meetings, substantive travel, preparation, participation, and substantial availability for Company matters.

To ensure an independent evaluation of the director candidates, the Board established a Special Committee on Election Matters, composed of independent directors Quyen Du and Ed Lu; Mr. Han was recused from such deliberations. After weighing the qualifications and fit of all candidates, the Board’s collective capabilities, and the Company’s current and foreseeable needs, the Special Committee determined that Mr. Han’s demonstrated contributions, independent judgment, and unique combination of capital markets, technology investments, legal, corporate finance, and transactional expertise, together with his governance and leadership experience and deep knowledge of Phunware and the 2.0 Strategy, made him the clear best choice. Continuity alone does not entitle a director to re-election, but it is extremely valuable at present because of Mr. Han’s specific experience, institutional knowledge of Phunware’s business, operating and management history, demonstrated leadership through periods of market and organizational transitions, oversight, and complementary fit as Chairperson and a member of the Board.

Why Replacing Mr. Han with Goldenwise’s Nominee Would Not Benefit Stockholders

The Special Committee is aware of Ms. Zhang’s qualifications and experience in investment management, capital allocation, and strategic advisory work. However, the materials provided and reviewed did not establish a sustained record of experience which the Board is focused on, including direct responsibility for commercial scaling, go-to-market experience, deep domain knowledge in hospitality and healthcare, AI, platform launches, executive management and operating leadership, and post-acquisition integration experience. In light of the Company’s needs and existing Board composition, these were and are important considerations for new directors as Phunware moves its AI-powered Guest Intelligence Platform and other components of Phunware 2.0 towards commercialization.

Ms. Zhang’s known public-company board experience consisted principally of approximately eight months on the board of Moberg Pharma, a company listed in Sweden. Although proposed for re-election, Ms. Zhang did not retain her seat at Moberg’s May 21, 2026 annual meeting, when stockholders elected an alternative slate that excluded her. Ms. Zhang's director questionnaire described her experience with investment and oversight frameworks, but the Committee did not find and Goldenwise has not shown sufficiently specific support for the proposition that her background and experience would improve Phunware’s product-market fit, technology expertise, commercialization milestones, or decisions about potential operating decisions or strategic alternatives. Also, her disclosed biography does not identify service on the board of a U.S.-listed company, and Goldenwise has not shown how her experience would strengthen the Board’s existing expertise in U.S. public-company governance and financing or in Phunware’s business.

The question for stockholders is not whether Ms. Zhang possesses useful professional qualifications. It is whether replacing Mr. Han with Ms. Zhang would strengthen the Board or improve the Company or its prospects, in particular the Company’s implementation of its 2.0 Strategy. The Committee concluded that her investment expertise and advisory background did not establish a sufficiently differentiated contribution in key areas of interest to the Board to offset the loss of Mr. Han’s demonstrated capital-markets, corporate legal, transaction, governance, and Phunware-specific experience or meet the anticipated operational needs in the Company’s next phase in the 2.0 Strategy. As such, the Committee supported and recommended Mr. Han’s renomination.

Progress Under Phunware’s 2.0 Strategy

Since February 2025, two new independent directors joined the Board: Quyen Du, formerly Head of Corporate Strategy and Development of Condé Nast, and Ed Lu, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer of Fandom. In May 2026, under Mr. Han’s Chairmanship, the Board appointed Dmitry Kroshka as Chief Executive Officer, ending a period of interim CEO leadership and establishing a clear direction for the Company's 2.0 Strategy.

Under the 2.0 Strategy, Phunware is bringing together its mobile, location-aware, and customer-engagement capabilities with AI to develop a shared intelligence platform for hospitality, healthcare, and other complex property verticals. We are excited about Phunware’s prospects under the 2.0 Strategy and believe it will be very beneficial to building long-term value for stockholders. Please see our stockholder letter released in October 2026, which can be accessed here, and our investor deck also posted in October 2026, which can be accessed here, for more information and detail on our 2.0 Strategy and recent milestones.

We have ample liquidity to implement and execute our 2.0 Strategy, including through inorganic growth opportunities. As of September 30, 2026, Phunware held approximately $86.7 million in cash and cash equivalents with no debt.

Your Board and management team remain focused on disciplined technology and data development, product sales and revenues, capital allocation and inorganic growth opportunities, demonstrating commercial progress, and keeping stockholders informed as we execute the 2.0 Strategy.

Goldenwise Has Not Presented a Specific Operating Plan or Alternative Strategy

We welcome stockholder input and recognize that every investor has the right to question our performance, strategy, and governance. However, a request for Board representation should be supported by a clear explanation of what would change and how stockholders would benefit.

Goldenwise has not proposed a specific operating plan or alternative strategy for Phunware’s business or growth or explained how its nominee would improve Phunware or its execution of the 2.0 Strategy. The Goldenwise materials provided so far are long on criticism and short on constructive substance. The Company invited Mr. Ding, on multiple occasions, to present specific proposals on product, strategy, acquisitions, capital allocation, and stockholder communications. To date, he has failed to present any such proposals. This is consistent with the pattern Goldenwise has shown throughout: demand Board representation, focus on broad generic themes that Phunware is already addressing, fail to engage on substance and details, and then accuse the Company of stonewalling.

Goldenwise’s demands for Board representation have shifted considerably. In April 2026, Mr. Ding urged the Board to add two or three directors. In June 2026, he proposed expanding the Board from three (3) to six (6) members and subsequently submitted four potential candidates, including himself. Goldenwise is now seeking to have one nominee elected to fill the single available seat. The number of seats sought has changed, but the demand for Board influence, without a specific operating plan or alternative strategy, reflects, in our view, an unfocused and undeveloped proposal. Stockholders should expect a clear, focused and developed plan and greater conviction from someone seeking to reshape the Board. As noted above, there is no need to reshape the Board to implement Phunware 2.0 with appropriate operating plan and budget: that will occur, and we welcome shareholder input on implementation of the adopted plan.

On broad themes and engagement, Goldenwise’s own proxy materials document discussions with the Company’s legal team on April 14, 2026, and meetings with the Board on May 15 and June 30, 2026, regarding those themes. The Company also prepared and offered to enter into a confidentiality agreement with Goldenwise and Mr. Ding to enable deeper discussions that could involve nonpublic information. Goldenwise’s proxy states that Mr. Ding declined on June 5, because the agreement might restrict further stock purchases or otherwise disadvantage stockholders. Confidentiality agreements of this kind are customary when an investor seeks access to nonpublic information. They protect all stockholders by ensuring that no single investor has access to information that other investors do not have when making trading decisions. Goldenwise’s later disclosures of short call and short put positions alongside its shareholdings reinforced, in the Company’s view, the importance of those protections. If Goldenwise and Mr. Ding signed the agreement, the Company believes the parties would have had a fuller and more meaningful dialogue.

Stockholders Deserve a Full and Accurate Context

Goldenwise’s criticisms of director compensation and leadership changes omit important details and context.

The August 2026 equity awards Goldenwise cites were granted under Phunware’s Outside Director Compensation Policy, which was adopted by the Board under a prior Chairperson who is no longer on the Board in June 2024 and benchmarked to market practice, well before Goldenwise began accumulating its reported position. The policy provides for non-discretionary annual director restricted stock unit awards with a stated value of $150,000. Goldenwise also mischaracterizes these awards by suggesting that these awards for Board service are discretionary, which they are not, and that these awards should have had an acquisition cost, which would be extremely uncommon and inconsistent with market practice.

Board compensation is also now paid in arrears rather than in advance for quarterly board services rendered, which further aligns directors with stockholders. Given Phunware’s internal resource challenges and the critical issues that it has been facing, Mr. Han and the other directors have consistently committed more time than is customary throughout their respective Board tenures.

On leadership changes, two of the three CEO transitions Goldenwise highlights occurred before Mr. Han became Chairperson in October 2025. The last two interim CEOs were appointed under the leadership of the above referenced prior Chairperson. The most recent CEO transition was the Board’s appointment of Dmitry Kroshka as permanent Chief Executive Officer in May 2026, under the leadership of Mr. Han as Chairperson, ending the interim leadership period. These distinctions matter when assessing the current Board leadership.

The Committee Also Considered Ms. Zhang’s Ties to Mr. Ding

The Special Committee considered Ms. Zhang’s professional and business relationships with Mr. Ding, including their overlapping service on the Moberg Pharma board and a sub-advisory arrangement between Ms. Zhang’s firm, Trunity Partners, and Goldenwise during 2025. These relationships require scrutiny when assessing whether she would as a Board member exercise judgment independently of the investor sponsoring her candidacy. Calling a nominee independent does not make her commercial ties to that investor irrelevant.

Mr. Ding’s record at Moberg Pharma also warrants scrutiny. Between August 13 and October 5, 2026, while remaining a director, he reported sales totaling 988,607 Moberg shares. Phunware stockholders should not confuse a demand for Board influence with a commitment to remain invested for the long term. By contrast, no current Phunware director has sold Phunware shares during his or her Board tenure (other than to cover taxes upon vesting of shares).

Goldenwise Demands Transparency While Its Own Record Raises Serious Questions

Goldenwise has called for greater transparency from the Board option positions, while its own disclosures to the Company leave serious gaps. In 2020 a complaint was filed in federal court naming Mr. Ding and Goldenwise Capital Management, Inc. as defendants, alleging professional negligence and breach of fiduciary duty arising from approximately $1.3 million in alleged investment losses over several days. This complaint is a matter of public record. Yet Mr. Ding submitted a signed director questionnaire to the Board (at a time when he was proposing himself and three (3) others for Board seats) answering “No” to a direct question asking whether, during the prior 10 years, he had been the subject of a legal proceeding involving breach of fiduciary duty, gross negligence, or similar conduct. In the Company’s view, this discrepancy raises questions about the completeness and accuracy of information provided to the Company in connection with the Goldenwise nominations. A demand for transparency by Goldenwise carries little weight without full candor from the person making it.

The disclosure concerns extend beyond the lawsuit. Mr. Ding’s signed questionnaire identified short call and short put options but provided insufficient detail to understand their terms and economic effect. Goldenwise’s July 10 and July 14 public filings did not describe those positions. Phunware publicly questioned these gaps on July 16. Four days later, Goldenwise added contract counts, strike prices, and expiration dates to its filing. Shareholders deserve an explanation for why fuller disclosure followed a public challenge from the Company. These positions also matter when assessing Mr. Ding’s claim of complete alignment with shareholders. Goldenwise’s October 20 filing disclosed short call options alongside long shares and short puts. Short calls can limit participation in a share price recovery above the strike price, while short puts can increase exposure to further declines. These arrangements can create different risks and rewards from those of shareholders who simply hold the stock. Before accepting Mr. Ding’s claim of complete alignment, shareholders deserve a full understanding of the financial interests behind his campaign.

Goldenwise May Seek Reimbursement for Its Campaign

Goldenwise estimates its solicitation costs at approximately $130,000 and stated that, if successful, it intends to seek reimbursement from Phunware, without submitting such reimbursement to a stockholder vote. Its campaign to reduce Company spending therefore comes with a potential bill for its own expenses.

Stockholders Have Significant Reason to be Cautious

The discrepancy in Mr. Ding’s director questionnaire, Ms. Zhang’s commercial ties to Goldenwise, and the absence of a specific operating plan or alternative strategy proposal, give stockholders significant reasons to be cautious and skeptical about entrusting Goldenwise’s nominee with a Board seat. Mr. Ding’s demand for influence should be tested against the accuracy of his own disclosures and the relevant experience and independence of his nominee. Goldenwise has given stockholders more reasons to question its campaign than to trust its nominee with a seat on the Board.

Stockholder Returns and the Case for Continuity

We recognize that Phunware’s recent share-price performance has been disappointing. We believe that as the Company implements the 2.0 Strategy the market will likely improve that performance. The Special Committee expressly considered stockholder returns in its assessment of Mr. Han, alongside the legacy business challenges, leadership transitions, and timing of the new strategy. Phunware 2.0 was approved in early 2026 and its broader leadership and advisory team was assembled in May 2026. The Committee nevertheless concluded that Mr. Han’s demonstrated contributions and relevant expertise make his continued service the best choice for Phunware stockholders.

We believe the current Board and management team have established a clear vision, strategy, and direction with Phunware 2.0 and that Mr. Han’s continued Board service is necessary to provide needed operational continuity, valuable oversight, and support to management as the Company steers Phunware forward from its legacy businesses to implement and execute on the 2.0 Strategy. Goldenwise has not demonstrated that replacing him would strengthen this Board or improve the Company’s prospects.

For these reasons, the Special Committee recommends that stockholders vote “FOR” the re-election of Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card at the 2026 Annual Meeting.

How to Vote

Phunware is using a universal proxy card, which lists the Board’s nominee and the Goldenwise nominee. Because only one director will be elected, please vote “FOR” only one nominee. Marking more than one will invalidate your vote on the election of the Class II director.

  • Vote “FOR” Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card or WHITE voting instruction form, by Internet, telephone or mail, following the instructions on the card. Internet votes by stockholders of record must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 16, 2026.
  • Discard any GOLD proxy card sent by Goldenwise. Signing and returning a later dated GOLD proxy card can revoke an earlier WHITE proxy card, even if you vote “WITHHOLD” on the GOLD card.
  • If you have already returned a GOLD card, you can change your vote by submitting a later-dated WHITE proxy card. Only your latest-dated proxy will be counted.
  • Even if you wish to vote for the Goldenwise nominee, the Board recommends that you use the WHITE proxy card to do so.
  • If you hold shares in more than one account, please vote each WHITE proxy card or voting instruction form you receive.

The Board also recommends that you vote “FOR” the ratification of CBIZ CPAs P.C. as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm for 2026, “FOR” the advisory vote to approve named executive officer compensation, and for “THREE YEARS” on the frequency of future advisory votes on executive compensation.

To attend the virtual 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, stockholders must register in advance at www.cesonlineservices.com/phun26_vm by 11:00 a.m. Eastern Time on December 16, 2026.

The 2.0 Strategy is in its first year. We ask for your support in giving that strategy the continuity it needs by voting “FOR” Elliot Han on the WHITE proxy card today.

Thank you for your continued support and investment in Phunware.

Sincerely,

The Special Committee on Election Matters of the Phunware Board of Directors
